blurb: Brother in Germanic; Latin frāter gave fraternal and fraternity, and French frère gave friar, a monk who is literally a brother.
Sun and Sunday grew from its n-form; Latin sōl gave solar, solstice and parasol; Greek hḗlios gave helium, first spotted in the sun's light.

meaning: fire (as a thing, not a living force)
blurb: Fire and bonfire in Germanic; Greek pûr gave pyre, pyrotechnics and pyromania.
Wind, weather and window (the Norse 'wind-eye'); Latin ventus gave vent and ventilate; Sanskrit nirvāṇa is the 'blowing out' of a flame.
Tree, true, trust and truce: things as firm as an oak. Greek drûs (oak) gave dryad; the Celtic druid was probably an 'oak-knower'.
Old English wer survives in werewolf and in world, 'the age of man'; Latin vir gave virile, virtue and virtuoso.
Year in Germanic; Greek hṓrā, 'season, hour', gave hour, horoscope and horology.
Red, ruddy and rust; Latin ruber gave ruby, rubric and rubella; French rouge; Greek eruthrós gave erythrocyte, the red blood cell.
Nose and nostril; Latin nāsus gave nasal and nasturtium, the 'nose-twister'.
Friend ('one who loves'), free (once 'beloved, one of the family') and Friday, the day of Frigg; Sanskrit priyá, 'dear'.
Love, lief and believe in Germanic; Latin libīdō, 'desire'; Russian lyubov', 'love'.
Word in Germanic; Latin verbum gave verb, verbal, verbose, adverb and proverb.
Read, riddle and rede (advice) in Germanic; Latin rērī, 'to reckon', gave reason, ratio, ration and rate.
East, Easter and Austria (Österreich, the 'eastern realm'); Latin aurōra and Greek Ēṓs, both the dawn.
Mouse in Germanic; Latin mūsculus, 'little mouse', gave muscle and mussel.
Fish in Germanic; Latin piscis gave Pisces, piscine and porpoise, the 'pig-fish'.
Farrow (a litter of piglets) in English; Latin porcus gave pork, porcupine ('spiny pig') and porpoise ('pig-fish'); Dutch varken gave aardvark, the 'earth-pig'.
